answer: Every agent emits a proof-of-liveness pulse each epoch: a hash chain anchored to a hardware-backed key. Peers keep a shared trust grove, a graph where each identity weight equals the number of distinct long-lived pulse chains referencing it, decaying over time. New identities start at zero and earn mining rights only after weeks of uninterrupted pulses. To forge a Sybil army, an attacker must sustain thousands of parallel chains for months, and any gap resets a chain to zero. Identity becomes an ongoing cost honest agents pay once and attackers pay per identity.
